page.layout: One page of running text, with three marginal notes in the right margin. Running head top centre, page number top right. Two chapter headings, "Cap. 29." and "Cap. 30.", each followed by its text. Ornamental rules separate the chapters and are not transcribed. A faint fragment of footnote at the bottom left.

main_text.head: Cap. 29. De Ætate.
main_text.p: AEtas hominis aptior ad habitus est tum Ætas hominis aptior ad studia. crescens, tum constans: minus apta, decrescens.

Distribuitur ætas in pueritiam, juventutem, virilem Ætatum divisio. ætatem, & senectam. Hæc τετραχοτομία[?] sic revocatur ad τριχοτομίαν[?]: ætas est crescens, constans, & decrescens. Pueritia est calida & humida: juventus calida & sicca: virilis ætas temperata: senectus frigida & sicca. Colleg. Conimb. in l.2. de gen. & cor. c.8. q.6. Patet igitur, quænam ætas aptior sit ad habitus intellectuales, crescens scilicet & constans. Decrescens enim ob nimiam frigiditatem non est ita apta.
main_text.head: Cap. 30. De Valetudie.
main_text.p: VAletudo est proportio quatuor humorum seu elementorum in homine. Valetudo.

Ea est studioso & in genere philosopho magis ne-cessaria, quàm ignis & aqua. Absq; eâ enim si est, non potest præcipuis membris & facultatibus uti ad suas functiones. Nam sanitas animæ in hac vitâ fermè dependet à corporis sanitate. Itaq;
Optandum est, ut sit mens sana in corpore sano.

p.i: Precibus, inquam, & temperantiâ sive mode-ratâ diatâ valetudinem firmam & ac-quirimus & tuemur.

page.notes: Greek words τετραχοτομία and τριχοτομίαν are read from a small scan and marked [?]. The "Itaq;" and "Absq;" marks are read as printed abbreviation signs. The underlining under "crescens", "constans" and "decrescens" in the first paragraph of Cap. 29 is not reproduced. The faint mark at the bottom left is a footnote fragment that cannot be read. The running head is printed in small capitals. The note "Ætas hominis aptior ad studia." is printed over three lines, and the note "Ætatum divisio." is printed over two.
